title: Root pairing from finite injective reflection data with spanning roots
statement:
Let $M,N$ be vector spaces over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], with a perfect bilinear pairing $p:M\times N\to\mathbf Q$: the induced linear maps $M\to N^\vee$ and $N\to M^\vee$ are isomorphisms, where $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q}(M,\mathbf Q)$. Let $I$ be finite, and let $a:I\hookrightarrow M$ and $b:I\hookrightarrow N$ be injective maps. Assume $p(a_i,b_i)=2$, that $p(a_i,b_j)$ is an integer for every $i,j$, that the $a_i$ span $M$, and that $s_i(x)=x-p(x,b_i)a_i$ maps $a(I)$ into $a(I)$. Then these prescribed families and $p$ extend to a crystallographic root pairing $P:\operatorname{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ in the Mathlib sense. Explicitly, its reflection permutations $\sigma_i:I\simeq I$ satisfy
$$a_{\sigma_i(j)}=a_j-p(a_j,b_i)a_i,\qquad b_{\sigma_i(j)}=b_j-p(a_i,b_j)b_i.$$
Both families span their respective spaces; in particular $P.\operatorname{IsRootSystem}$ holds. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed. The empty families in $M=N=0$ are permitted. Vector-space bases and dimension use [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].
